name: Donets Steppe Front
inspired_by: The Donbas front in eastern Ukraine as of 2026, where full-scale war continues despite truce attempts: open black-earth steppe cut into fields by tree-line windbreaks, coal-mining towns with slag heaps (terrikons) and Soviet panel blocks, chalk hills, a river with pine forest on its sandy bank, and a front line shaped by drones, minefields and trench systems. Frontline towns are largely evacuated and heavily damaged. All towns are fictional.
climate: Humid continental to semi-arid steppe (Koppen Dfa/Dfb). Hot summers (28-35 C), cold winters (-5 to -15 C) with variable snow; 450-550 mm precipitation; spring and autumn rasputitsa mud seasons.
seasons: Winter (Dec-Feb): frozen ground, snow cover some years, bare tree lines give drones a clear view
Late spring and summer (May-Sep): tree lines in leaf (concealment), dust, wheat and sunflower fields, field fires
Autumn (Oct-Nov): leaf fall, mud returns, fog

vegetation: wheat, sunflower and maize fields (many abandoned and overgrown near the front)
windbreak tree lines of black locust, ash, poplar and oak
weeds and steppe grass on fallow
birch and sea buckthorn on slag heaps
reed and willow on the banks

terrain.relief: Rolling steppe plateau (180-330 m) dissected by ravines (balky) and gullies; a river valley (50-80 m) with steep right-bank chalk bluffs and a flat sandy left bank under pine; conical and flat-topped slag heaps up to 80-100 m above the surrounding ground near mines.
features: windbreak tree lines dividing fields into 0.5-1 km blocks
a river with destroyed bridges and pontoon crossings
trench systems, dugouts and anti-tank ditches
terrain.water: One river crossing the map (40-100 m wide) with a reservoir upstream, ponds in ravine bottoms (stavky), canals; the river is the main obstacle.

generator.approach: Heightmap at 10 m. Plateau from low-frequency fbm; ravines carved by flow accumulation with steep sides; river valley carved as an asymmetric spline (steep right bank, gentle left); slag heaps stamped as cones and truncated cones near mine POIs; tree lines placed as a vector grid along field boundaries (not heightmap). A war-damage pass adds craters (cellular), trench lines and rubble per front proximity.

noise_layers.purpose: artillery crater fields, density scaled by distance to the front

generator.erosion: Hydraulic erosion for ravine heads and chalk gullies; none on fields.
generator.rivers: River spline with an asymmetric valley; reservoir behind a dam stamp; ravine ponds at dammed gully mouths.
generator.settlement_flattening: Towns flattened per block; villages along ravine bottoms per plot; mine complexes as flattened pads.
generator.notes: The front is a 2-4 km wide 'grey zone' band across the map where drones dominate: any vehicle movement in daylight is detected. Tree lines are the main cover; ravines the main covered routes. The damage pass is factual in scale (front towns heavily destroyed) without depicting specific real events.

settlements.architecture: Mining town: five- and nine-storey Soviet panel and brick apartment blocks, a palace of culture with columns, a mine headframe and processing plant, two-storey Stalin-era houses, a central square with a monument plinth; most buildings damaged, windows boarded, upper floors collapsed.
settlements.wall_class: Panel and brick blocks thick (basements are shelters); upper floors collapse in stages; private houses thin.
layout_rules: grid of microdistricts around a central square
mine and slag heap on the edge
private-house sector (chastnyi sektor) of single-storey houses with gardens around the core

settlements.architecture: Steppe villages along ravines: single-storey houses of brick or plastered adobe with gabled roofs of asbestos-cement slate or tin, painted fences, summer kitchens, sheds and cellars, gardens; a shop, a school, a church with blue or gold domes; many damaged and abandoned near the front.
settlements.wall_class: Brick medium; adobe thin-medium; cellars thick (shelters).
layout_rules: single or double street along a ravine with a pond
gardens and orchards behind each house
tree lines lead out to the fields

settlements.architecture: Industrial city edge: a large steel or chemical plant with concrete halls, chimneys and rail sidings; high-rise blocks; shopping centre.
settlements.wall_class: Plant halls thick walls but thin roofs; underground utility tunnels as level geometry.
layout_rules: plant on the river with rail sidings

settlements.architecture: Military positions: trench systems with dugouts roofed with logs and earth, fortified tree-line positions, camouflaged artillery positions, anti-drone netting over roads, dragon's teeth and anti-tank ditches behind the front, logistics hubs in farm buildings.
settlements.wall_class: Dugouts and log-earth roofs thick; nets none.
layout_rules: positions along tree lines and ravine edges
anti-drone net tunnels over the last km of supply roads

infrastructure.roads: A highway (cratered, with netting tunnels on stretches), regional roads, field tracks along tree lines; most bridges over the river destroyed, replaced by pontoon and improvised crossings.
infrastructure.rail: Electrified line with a junction station, damaged; rail bridge down.
infrastructure.power: Grid destroyed near the front; generators; a damaged thermal power station on the reservoir.
infrastructure.airfields: None usable (AI aircraft only from off-map).
infrastructure.checkpoints: Military checkpoints on all roads into the front band; the grey zone has none.

pois.description: Front-line village with collapsed houses; a few elderly residents in cellars; trenches through gardens.
pois.contract_use: evacuate civilians from a front village (client ukr)

pois.description: Fortified tree-line position: trench, dugouts, firing points, anti-drone net; 1 km of open field to the next tree line.
Observation post dug into a slag heap with views across the front; very exposed to drones.
Crashed reconnaissance or long-range drone in a field between tree lines; mines nearby.
pois.contract_use: recover downed drone or sensitive kit (client ukr)

pois.description: Pontoon bridge over the river under netting, a ferry point and a hidden vehicle park in pine forest.
pois.contract_use: night convoy escort (client ukr); sabotage logistics (client ukr, on the opposing crossing)

pois.description: Coal mine: headframe tower, winding house, processing plant, conveyor galleries, railway loading bunkers.
Air-defence and electronic-warfare site in a farm: radar, jammers, gun trucks, a generator.
Supply hub in a collective-farm hangar: fuel bowsers, ammunition stacks under nets, workshops.
pois.contract_use: sabotage logistics (enemy hub, client ukr); defend a hub

pois.description: Marked minefield belt across fields with tripwire warnings and burnt vehicle hulks; game hazard that channels movement.
Large columned Soviet culture house in the town square, damaged roof, basement used as a command post.
pois.contract_use: HVT capture (enemy command post); hot-zone HQ

pois.description: White chalk quarry with terraces, tunnels and machinery; dazzling in sun, shows dark uniforms.
Industrial plant with halls, chimneys, underground utility tunnels and rail sidings; a defensive fortress.

weather.visibility_notes: Fog and low cloud are the only time drones are limited, which makes them the preferred windows for movement; winter bare tree lines expose positions; thermal sights see through smoke.
weather.dust_or_snow: Dust in summer on tracks; snow some winters.

civilians.behaviour: Front-line towns and villages largely evacuated: a few elderly residents remain in cellars; volunteers and police evacuate them in armoured vans. Rear towns have normal life with air-raid alerts sending people to shelters. Civilians near the front move only in short dashes between shelters.
civilians.casualty_risk_notes: Low density, but the remaining civilians are in the same cellars and buildings soldiers use; artillery and drone strikes by other factions do not count against the player.

factions_present.where: Western half: tree-line positions, the river crossings, mining town, counter-drone sites, rear villages; drone units everywhere.
Eastern half: assault groups along tree lines, artillery positions, logistics hubs, command posts in town buildings; drones everywhere.
Russian rear: an attached KPA artillery and engineer contingent at the east edge (proposed game placement).
Russian-side assault groups and drone teams on the east side of the front; sabotage teams behind the Ukrainian line.
No Belarusian units on this front in reality; appears only as Russian-attached logistics and training cadre at the east edge (plausibility flagged).

frontline: An attritional front across the middle of the map. The war sim advances it in small steps (a tree line, a village street) after assault events; the grey zone between positions is 1-4 km wide and dominated by drones. Each captured tree line moves the front by 0.5-1 km; towns flip block by block. Weather windows (fog) increase assault events. Ukrainian contracts focus on counter-drone defence, evacuation, logistics escort, recovery and recon; raids are short and high-risk. Truce events (campaign calendar) freeze the line and post demining and evacuation contracts.
contract_hooks: Counter-drone site defence at a farm EW site (client ukr)
Recover a downed drone or sensitive kit between tree lines (client ukr)
Evacuate civilians from a front village cellar (client ukr)
Night convoy escort across the pontoon crossing (client ukr)
Trench raid on a tree-line position (client ukr)
Sabotage an enemy logistics hub (client ukr)
Demining route escort for engineers (client ukr)
HVT capture at an enemy command post in the town (client ukr, late)
Defend against KPA assault groups at the east edge (client ukr)

hot_zones.name: Mining town sector
hot_zones.layout: rus HQ in the palace of culture basement; 5-6 outposts in tree lines and blocks; checkpoints on two roads behind their line; roaming assault pairs and drone teams; 2 QRF groups with armoured vehicles and cope cages; Ukrainian positions as the friendly anchor

insertion.fob: FOB in a rear village 15-20 km from the front (off the map's west edge), reached by road; final approach on foot or in armoured vans at night. Helicopters are not used near the front (proposed: too dangerous); no AAVs.

early_game_notes: High-intensity state war (rus late tier); late-campaign theatre.
proposed: war-damage pass scaled by front proximity
front advance rules (tree line steps, block-by-block towns)
